note: Telangana State Board (SCERT Telangana / Board of Secondary Education, Telangana). SOURCES: scert.telangana.gov.in was reachable and hosts the actual textbook PDFs at scert.telangana.gov.in/pdf/publication/ebooks(2019)/ — every chapter list in this catalog was fetched directly from an official English-medium SCERT Telangana textbook PDF downloaded from that domain (marked 'fetched:<url>' per subject); bse.telangana.gov.in was also reached but hosts only exam-administration content, not textbooks or syllabi, so it contributed nothing directly. No secondary sources were needed for chapter titles: every subject/grade below is traced to the government's own PDF (either its printed table of contents/INDEX page or, where a table layout garbled in PDF-to-text extraction, cross-checked against the chapter-opening title printed on the book's own pages). Because this is a stronger source position than the AP catalog achieved (whose official portal was unreachable), every subject here is 'fetched:', not 'fetched-secondary:' or 'model-knowledge' — this catalog has no model-knowledge chapter lists. SUBJECT MAPPING: Telangana runs a single combined 'Science' textbook for Class 6 and Class 7 (id 'science'), then splits it from Class 8 into two separate subjects/books exactly as suspected — 'Physical Science' (Physics + Chemistry, id 'physical_science') and 'Biology' (id 'biological_science') — confirmed directly from the official Class 8, 9 and 10 Physical Science and Biology PDFs, which are printed and distributed as distinct books with their own covers. Social Studies is one combined subject (id 'social') across all grades. COMPUTER SCIENCE: Telangana does distribute a 'Digital Learning' book for Classes VI-X (coding, computational thinking, Python, Raspberry Pi/Arduino, AI, data science, digital citizenship — a real and notably more ambitious program than AP has), confirmed via SCERT-adjacent secondary coverage (teachersbadi.in per-class pages) and one official curricular-subject PDF on scert.telangana.gov.in (ICT_IX.pdf, dated 2015 and likely superseded). It is INTENTIONALLY OMITTED as a structured subject here: repeated searches turned up only thematic topic lists ('Coding', 'AI', 'Data Science' as broad areas) and never a stable, numbered chapter-by-chapter table of contents comparable in reliability to Math/Science/Social, and no source could confirm whether it is formally examined with marks (like Math or Science) versus assessed only through in-class formative activities. Rather than invent chapter titles for a subject whose own structure isn't publicly nailed down, it is left out — following the AP catalog's precedent of documenting an omission instead of fabricating content. STRUCTURAL DIVERGENCE FROM AP: Telangana's Social Studies for Classes 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 diverge sharply from AP's NCERT-aligned Social Studies — Telangana kept the older 'position paper' structure built around Telangana-specific case-study villages (Penamakuru, Dokur, Penugolu in Class 6), Telugu-region history (the Kakatiyas, Vijayanagara), and its own Class 9-10 Political Science/Economics sequence (Parts I & II) that culminates in Class 10 with a dedicated chapter, 'The Movement for the Formation of Telangana State' — material AP's textbooks obviously do not carry. Telangana's Class 8 Social Studies book is also markedly shorter (12 chapters) than AP's Class 8 Social Studies book (24 chapters); Telangana appears to have trimmed the same base content down rather than dropped it, since its first 12 chapters are titled identically to AP's first 12. Telangana's Class 6 Science (16 chapters, fetched across two official 'part-1'/'part-2' PDFs) and Class 6 Social Studies (21 chapters, also two official parts) both run notably longer than AP's equivalents. By contrast, Class 9 Mathematics and the Class 10 Mathematics sequence (including Sets, Similar Triangles and Tangents and Secants to a Circle) are — chapter-for-chapter — identical to AP's, indicating both states still share a common, largely unrevised Mathematics curriculum post-2014 bifurcation even though their Science and Social Studies curricula have diverged. EDITION / VINTAGE CAVEATS: PDFs were fetched at whatever is the latest edition currently linked from scert.telangana.gov.in as of 2026-07-07; for subjects with a 2024-25-dated PDF (Mathematics all grades, Class 7 Science, Class 8-9 Physical Science, Class 8 Biology, Class 9 Social Studies) this is very likely the current in-use edition. For subjects where only an undated or older-dated PDF was linked (Class 6 Science/Social 2022-23, Class 7/8 Social 2020-21/2022-23, Class 8 Mathematics 2020-21, Class 9/10 Biology and Class 10 Physical Science/Social undated, printed 2019-22), no newer edition could be found via search, so these are treated as still current, but with slightly lower confidence that a very recent silent revision hasn't occurred. CONFIDENCE: high across the board given every chapter list traces to an official PDF; specific full-confidence over lower-confidence notes: Class 9 Biology chapters 5, 8 and 9 (Diversity in Living Organisms, Challenges in Improving Agricultural Products, Adaptations in Different Ecosystems) were read from the book's own INDEX table rather than cross-verified against a chapter-opening title page like the other 8 chapters in that book, because pdftotext's column extraction skipped straight past their opening pages — still official-source, just one layer less redundantly checked.
